note: Regulatory changes, enforcement orders and pending bills. Pending bills are NOT law until passed and notified.

items.title: ED arrests alleged mastermind of ₹200 crore CSR diversion case under PMLA
items.summary: After the special court's nod, the Enforcement Directorate in Mumbai arrested the Class XII-pass man accused of posing as a doctor and channelling about ₹200 crore of PSU and private CSR money through trusts and shell entities, with several funded projects allegedly never delivered. Allegations only; no conviction yet.

items.title: ITAT Ahmedabad quashes revision over ₹31.68 crore Section 80G claim on CSR donations (Axis Bank, AY 2020-21)
items.summary: The Tribunal set aside the Principal Commissioner's Section 263 order. It held that the CSR bar in Explanation 2 to Section 37(1) does not cut down a separate Section 80G deduction, and that the verification point was raised for the first time in revision. Donations to Swachh Bharat Kosh and Clean Ganga Fund remain outside 80G.

items.title: PMLA court lets ED formally arrest alleged mastermind of ₹200 crore CSR diversion case
items.summary: A special PMLA court in Mumbai allowed the ED to arrest Juhu resident Dharmendra Singh, who allegedly posed as a doctor and ran trusts that drew CSR money from about 40 PSUs, public sector banks and private firms and routed it through linked entities. Probe continues; a reminder to verify implementing agencies before releasing CSR funds.

items.title: Draft CSR Rules would also shrink the heritage item and bar most in-kind CSR
items.summary: Analysis of the 11 Nov 2026 draft notes it limits the heritage entry to preservation and protection (dropping historical sites and promotion of traditional art), counts in-kind contributions only for disaster relief, deletes the COVID-19 R&D entry and requires implementing agencies to report CSR-1 changes within 30 days. Comments due 11 Dec 2026. Draft only.

items.title: ITAT Bangalore: CSR donation to Karnataka CM Relief Fund still qualifies for Section 80G (Adcock Ingram, AY 2020-21)
items.summary: An 80G deduction of about ₹1.44 crore was allowed: an otherwise eligible donation cannot be refused only because it counted as CSR, since the Section 37(1) bar applies to business-income computation. The revision under Section 263 was quashed as the officer had already examined the claim.

items.title: MCA draft Companies (CSR Policy) Amendment Rules, 2026 released for consultation
items.summary: Proposes new exclusions (one-off events, government schemes, corpus contributions, own products in kind), voluntary impact assessment, and surrender/cancellation of implementing-agency registration with a 3-year bar. Comments till 11 Dec 2026. Not yet in force.

items.title: MCA draft replaces Schedule VII with a 14-item list of CSR activities
items.summary: Adds mental health, telemedicine, PM Internship Scheme, career counselling, e-waste, marine resources and sports items; groups PM CARES, PMNRF and other funds; asks for liberal interpretation. Draft only.

items.title: ITAT Mumbai quashes Section 263 revision over Section 80G claim on CSR donations (NTT Global Data Centers, AY 2020-21)
items.summary: The tax commissioner had reopened the assessment, arguing CSR spending is not a donation. The Tribunal held that the Section 37(1) bar on deducting CSR as business expense does not by itself block an independent Section 80G claim; only gifts to Swachh Bharat Kosh and Clean Ganga Fund are excluded. Revision set aside. Adds to the run of ITAT rulings allowing 80G on qualifying CSR gifts.

items.title: ITAT Mumbai upholds Section 80G relief on CSR-linked donations (Asian Paints, AY 2020-21)
items.summary: Dismissing the Revenue's appeal, the Tribunal confirmed the CIT(A)'s order allowing an 80G claim of about ₹37.8 crore on CSR donations, reading Explanation 2 to Section 37(1) as limited to business expenditure and not to Chapter VI-A deductions.

items.title: ITAT Mumbai quashes Section 263 revision on 80G claim for CSR donations (Rishabh Instruments, AY 2020-21)
items.summary: The Tribunal held that disallowing CSR spend as a business expense does not automatically deny a separate 80G deduction (about ₹10.5 lakh claimed), and that the assessing officer had taken a plausible view after examining the papers.

items.title: UK FCA finalises rules bringing ESG rating providers under regulation (PS26/22)
items.summary: Authorisation gateway opens June 2027; regime in force from 29 June 2028.

items.title: MCA widens overseas listing rules to equity instruments (G.S.R. 968(E))
items.summary: Companies (Listing of equity instruments in permissible jurisdictions) Amendment Rules, 2026 extend scope beyond equity shares to convertibles and preference shares and bring IFSC unlisted public companies in. Not CSR-specific.

items.title: ITAT Jaipur: CSR donations eligible for Section 80G, revision quashed (Gillette India, AY 2018-19)
items.summary: On CSR spend of about ₹4.34 crore with an 80G claim of about ₹1.77 crore, the Tribunal held Section 80G works independently of Section 37(1), so a donation meeting 80G conditions is not disqualified for also satisfying Section 135.

items.title: MCA General Circular 05/2026 extends FY 2025-26 annual filings without extra fees
items.summary: AOC-4 to 31 Dec 2026; MGT-7/7A to 31 Jan 2027. AGM dates not extended. CSR-2 is not mentioned in summaries, so check before relying on it.

items.title: ITAT Mumbai upholds Section 80G deduction on CSR donations (Viterra India, AY 2020-21)
items.summary: The tribunal quashed a Section 263 revision that sought to deny ₹1.43 crore of 80G deduction on CSR payments to PM CARES and six institutions, holding the AO had enquired adequately. CSR itself stays non-deductible under Section 37(1); the 80G question is still litigated, so check your own facts.

items.title: ED searches 8 locations in ₹200 crore CSR donation laundering case
items.summary: PMLA case: trusts allegedly took CSR from ~40 PSUs and banks and recycled funds via shell entities.

items.title: EU revised ESRS and voluntary standard for non-CSRD companies published in the Official Journal
items.summary: Delegated Regulations (EU) 2026/1563 (simplified ESRS, in force 10 Nov 2026, mandatory for financial years from 1 Jan 2027) and 2026/1560 (voluntary standard for out-of-scope companies) complete Omnibus I. Relevant to Indian groups with EU subsidiaries or EU customers asking for ESG data.

items.title: ITAT Panaji allows ₹2.09 crore Section 80G deduction on CSR donations (Colorcon Asia, AY 2020-21)
items.summary: Out of ₹4.41 crore CSR spend, the company claimed ₹2.09 crore under Section 80G; the Revenue denied it on the view that mandatory CSR is not a donation. The Tribunal allowed the claim since none of it went to Swachh Bharat Kosh or Clean Ganga Fund.

items.title: JPC report on the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 tabled
items.summary: Backs raising the CSR net-profit trigger from ₹5 crore to ₹10 crore, and recommends removing the government's power to revise that threshold.

items.title: ROC Mumbai II penalises Royal Foodstuffs for FY 2023-24 CSR shortfall
items.summary: Suo-motu application; ₹34.08 lakh FY 2023-24 obligation not met; ₹14.16 lakh penalty on the company plus officers under Section 135(7).

items.title: ROC Mumbai II also penalises Royal Foodstuffs for FY 2020-21 unspent CSR
items.summary: ₹5.51 lakh not transferred by Sep 2021; ₹11.02 lakh on the company and ₹55,092 on each of two directors.

items.title: ROC Cuttack penalises Malook Chand Foods for late Form CSR-2 (FY 2020-21)
items.summary: CSR-2 due June 2022 was filed only in June 2026; late filing did not cure the continuing default. ₹2 lakh on the company and ₹50,000 on each of three officers under Section 450.

items.title: ROCs issue show-cause notices to companies that never filed Form CSR-2 for FY 2021-22
items.summary: Orders cite a Ministry instruction on CSR non-compliance — a signal that CSR-2 non-filers are being flagged systematically.

items.title: ROC Delhi II penalises Varindera Constructions for late transfer of unspent CSR (FY 2020-21)
items.summary: ₹5.20 lakh unspent was moved to a Schedule VII fund years late; company and five officers penalised.

items.title: ROC Cuttack issues three orders for CSR-2 filed four years late (FY 2020-21)
items.summary: Khemka Refractories, Gurumahraj Engicon and Kashvi Power & Steel each fined ₹2 lakh plus ₹50,000 per officer under Section 450; filing the form before adjudication and later-appointed company secretaries did not avoid the penalty.

items.title: ROCs penalise wrong 'CSR not applicable' declarations in AOC-4 XBRL
items.summary: ROC Kolkata (M Rajkrishna Trading) and ROC Mumbai (Robinsons Cargo, Arihant Innochem) fined companies/directors where an incorrect CSR flag in AOC-4 blocked filing of CSR-2; a later GNL-1 rectification request did not cure the breach.

items.title: ROC Bilaspur penalises late CSR-2 filing even after the company filed before the notice
items.summary: Filing late (before the SCN) did not avoid a penalty under Section 450.

items.title: ITAT Bangalore allows Section 80G deduction on mandatory CSR spend (Schneider Electric IT Business India, AY 2020-21)
items.summary: The tribunal set aside the denial of an 80G claim of about ₹3.76 crore on CSR donations, treating it as a double disallowance since CSR spend was already added back under Section 37. Adds to a line of ITAT rulings allowing 80G on CSR contributions to approved bodies.

items.title: ITAT Delhi allows Section 80G deduction on CSR donations (Cosmo First, AY 2021-22)
items.summary: The tribunal rejected the AO/DRP view that a Section 135 mandate makes CSR donations involuntary, and allowed the 80G claim. Adds to the line of rulings that CSR spend can still qualify for 80G if the donee and conditions are met.

items.title: CSR Amendment Rules 2026: new Rule 4A and Schedule VII item (xiii) for Social Stock Exchange ZCZP instruments
items.summary: Up to 10% of a year's CSR spend may go into ZCZP instruments; no impact assessment needed for those projects.

items.title: ITAT allows ₹22.60 lakh 80G relief on CSR donation despite Section 37 bar (Genesys International, AY 2020-21)
items.summary: A donation to an approved foundation, disallowed as a business expense because it was CSR, was held eligible for Section 80G: the Section 37 Explanation 2 restriction does not block the separate 80G deduction.

items.title: Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 introduced in Lok Sabha and sent to a JPC
items.summary: CSR proposals: ₹10 crore profit trigger, 90 days (from 30) to fund the Unspent CSR Account, committee exemption raised to ₹1 crore.

items.title: EU Council gives final approval to Omnibus I (CSRD/CSDDD simplification)
items.summary: CSRD scope narrows to >1,000 employees and >€450m turnover; wave 2 pushed back two years.

items.title: A Companies (Amendment) Bill, 2025 introduced in Rajya Sabha proposes LOWER CSR thresholds
items.summary: Proposes net worth ₹100 crore, turnover ₹500 crore, net profit ₹3 crore — the opposite direction to the 2026 Bill. Watch both.

items.title: Revised e-Form CSR-1 for registering implementing agencies takes effect
items.summary: More detailed documentation and professional certification for CSR-1 registration.

items.title: SEBI eases BRSR Core: 'assessment or assurance', value-chain disclosure deferred, green credits added
items.summary: Listed entities may pick third-party assessment instead of assurance; value-chain ESG disclosure deferred.
